market_news.paragraph: Global equities were broadly weaker in the latest completed round of trading, with 8 of the 24 benchmarks tracked on this page closing higher. In the United States, the S&P 500 fell 0.40 per cent to 7,561.67, the Dow Jones rose 0.10 per cent to 52,348, the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.91 per cent to 25,136 and the Russell 2000 fell 0.31 per cent to 2,790.49. In Europe, the FTSE 100 rose 0.36 per cent to 10,903, the DAX fell 0.08 per cent to 26,750 and the CAC 40 rose 0.09 per cent to 8,368.91. Across Asia, the Nikkei 225 fell 2.35 per cent to 59,706, the Hang Seng rose 0.61 per cent to 23,782, the KOSPI fell 4.05 per cent to 5,076.06, the Shanghai Composite fell 0.95 per cent to 3,599.86, the BSE Sensex rose 0.41 per cent to 81,927 and the Straits Times fell 0.78 per cent to 5,190.92. Elsewhere, the Ibovespa rose 0.66 per cent to 172,458. Locally, the S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.41 per cent to 9,044.70 and the All Ordinaries fell 0.42 per cent to 9,165.40. In digital assets, bitcoin changed hands at $64,319, up 0.21 per cent over the past 24 hours. In currencies, the US dollar bought 1.4738 Australian dollars, up 0.53 per cent against the prior business day's fix. Index levels, exchange rates and commodity prices on this page are captured live at build time from the sources linked in each section; no forward-looking view is offered here.
